subject: Velotech: request for tenant-level cache isolation & warm-pool guarantee
messages:
From: Joanna Park <joanna.park@velotech.io>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Request: tenant cache isolation + warm pool guarantee for POC

Connor —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Velotech is excited to move toward a small pilot (POC) for our fraud-detection feature. Before we sign the SOW, our infra and security teams have two asks that are gating acceptance:

1) Tenant-level KV/cache isolation (we need eviction control per tenant so our KV state can't be evicted by noisy neighbors).
2) A warm-pool guarantee for our traffic window (we need predictable cold-start behavior during the first 90 days).

We understand these are product asks, but both are deal-level requirements for us due to latency SLAs with our bank partners. We attached the SOW and a short performance matrix. Target go-live: 2027-04-15.

Can your team confirm whether Redwood can commit to either of these in time for the POC? If not, what mitigations are realistic?

Happy to jump on a call this week — procurment is watching timelines closely.

Thanks,
Joanna Park
Head of Platform Engineering
Velotech

Attachments: Velotech_SOW_v2.pdf, velotech-performance-matrix.xlsx
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Joanna Park <joanna.park@velotech.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: tenant cache isolation + warm pool guarantee for POC

Joanna —

Appreciate the clear ask and the SOW. Quick acknowledgement: we can support a POC and will get product + eng aligned on feasibility on an accelerated timeline. Looping in Karthik (AE) and Monica (CS) to coordinate.

Karthik / Monica — Velotech is asking for two deal-critical behaviors (tenant-level KV eviction control and a warm pool SLA for the first 90 days). They are targeting 2027-04-15 go-live. Can product/eng advise on scope and whether we can commit any fallback (partial guarantees, canary fallback to lower-latency variants, manual warm-up playbooks)?

I can set up a quick triage slot tomorrow (30 min).

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Velotech POC — priority ask and commercial context

Markus / Maya —

Quick context before a triage call: Velotech is a mid-enterprise prospect in discussions for a 12-month commitment. ARR estimate (if we convert): ~$420k/year. SOW includes a 90-day pilot followed by activation. Procurement has pushed 4/15 as pilot start — they will push for penalties if we miss timings.

They have two technical asks (listed below). From a commercial perspective, this is a high-probability close if we can either: (A) provide a short-term operational guarantee + product roadmap commitment, or (B) ship a low-risk mitigation (e.g., pinned warm instances + runtime config to reduce KV eviction).

As this is a cross-functional escalation, request the following from product/eng in 24 hours:
- A short assessment of effort + risk for tenant-level KV eviction control (rough T-shirt estimate: S, M, L)
- Whether we can offer a temporary warm-pool guarantee (manual ops + reserved warm pool) and the associated monthly cost to Velotech (so we can price it into the SOW)

Connor / Monica are on deck to coordinate the procurement timeline.

Karthik
Account Executive — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Velotech POC — priority ask and commercial context

Team —

Thanks for the context. High-level assessment below (timeline estimates assume we divert a small eng squad and deprioritize a lower-risk backlog):

1) Tenant-level KV eviction control:
- Scope: add per-tenant eviction weighting + an API surface to pin keys (requires changes to runtime cache manager and control-plane config).
- T-shirt estimate: Medium (approx 3–4 sprints of a focused eng squad for initial implementation + testing).
- Risk: medium — requires careful KV lifecycle testing and adding safety knobs to avoid memory bloat.

2) Warm-pool guarantee:
- Scope: operationally we can reserve warm instances for a customer (Dedicated warm hosts + pre-warmed KV). Implementing a formal SLA + automated warm-pool orchestration is larger (Large).
- Short-term mitigation: Ops-run reserved warm pool (manual runbook) for the POC window (can be priced).

Recommended path for POC (minimize delivery risk):
- Offer an ops-backed warm pool for the 90-day pilot (we charge a fixed monthly amount for reserved capacity — finance to price).
- Deliver a roadmap commitment for per-tenant eviction controls: M-priority with a target beta by end of Q2 (we can commit a code deliverable sightline).

I'll prepare a short note for commercial: proposed interim SOW clause for reserved warm-pool + roadmap commitment with acceptance criteria (we keep this narrow: e.g., ability to set per-tenant eviction weight and a small API to pin critical keys).

Markus Klein
Head of Product — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-runtime-eviction-notes.md (internal), will follow up with a draft SOW clause and cost estimate.
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Velotech POC — priority ask and commercial context

Following up with engineering constraints & a narrow technical plan. Quoting Markus below for context.

> 1) Tenant-level KV eviction control:
> - Scope: add per-tenant eviction weighting + an API surface to pin keys
> - T-shirt estimate: Medium (3–4 sprints)

Concretely: initial implementation plan (minimum viable for POC) — 6-week scoped work if we reallocate one full backend engineer + one runtime engineer and move two lower-priority tasks. Deliverables:
- Control-plane flag to assign a tenant eviction weight (int 1–100)
- Runtime config to reserve a small KV slab per tenant (configurable bytes)
- A simple API to pin/unpin up to N keys per tenant (N configurable)
- Integration test harness and perf run for 95th percentile latency impact

Risks & mitigations:
- Memory pressure if weights misconfigured — mitigation: default global caps + auto-eviction thresholds; require CS to opt-in for reserved slabs per SOW.
- Performance regressions — mitigation: perf tests + canary rollout to pilot tenant only.

Warm-pool (short-term): Ops can provision a dedicated warm pool of instances and seed KV before peak windows. Approx estimated ops cost to Velotech: $6k/month for reserved warm capacity for the pilot (ballpark; finance to confirm). This avoids shipping SLA automation immediately.

If commercial agrees to the reserved-warm fee and a clear acceptance test for the eviction API, engineering can commit to the 6-week MV implementation and a separate workstream to harden the feature for GA.

Next steps:
- Karthik / Connor: confirm whether Velotech will accept a priced reserved-warm offer for the pilot and a roadmap commitment with beta target (end of Q2).
- Monica: if accepted, we'll prepare a short opt-in runbook for Ops and an internal change request.

Thanks,
Maya Srinivasan
Senior Staff Engineer — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
